1. Both these applications are preferred by the
 applicants who are husband and relatives of the husband for
 quashing of First Information Report in connection with Crime
 No.1132/2020, registered with Police Station Mangrulpir,
 District Washim, for the offences punishable under Sections
 498A, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

2.  The applicants who are the husband and the  relatives of the husband are arraigned as an accused on the  basis of her report lodged by the informant/non-applicant No.2  on an allegations that her marriage was performed with  applicant No.1/Vaibhav Bapurao Jadhao   Application (APL) No.146/2021 as per the Hindu Rites and  Customs.
After the marriage she resumed cohabitation at the  926-apl146.21 & 28.21.odt 2/6  house of applicants and she was treated well initially for four Vanita W/

sentences.text: However she was co-habiting at the house of the present  applicants under the expectations some day everything will be  all rights, but there was no change in behavior of the present  applicants and she was ill-treated to the extent that she was  constrained to leave the matrimonial house.
On the basis of  said report Police have registered the crime against the present  applicants.
3. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, who
submitted that on perusal of the entire F.I.R. it reveals that all  the relatives of the husband were arraigned as an accused  though they are residing at different places.
They never resides  along with the husband of the informant or other inlaws.

She  further invited our attention towards the recitals of the F.I.R.
 and submitted that the allegations are of real and tear in nature  regarding day to day homely affairs of the informant and her  husband.

She submitted that even accepting the allegations as  it is at its face value no offence is made out as far as the offence  under Section 498A is concerned as the entire allegations are  vague, general in nature.
No specific instances are narrated by  the informant.
Therefore, continuing the proceeding against  the present applicants would be an abuse of process of law.
In  view of that, the application deserves to be allowed.

4. Per contra, learned Additional Public Prosecutor  strongly opposed the said application and submitted that  considering the allegations levelled against the present  applicants which shows that prima facie case is made out  926-apl146.21 & 28.21.odt 3/6  against them who have harassed her for various reasons and,
 therefore, the application deserves to be rejected.
 5.

Learned counsel for the non-applicant No.2 also  reiterated the said contentions and submitted that considering  the nature of the allegations prima facie case is made out and,
 therefore, the application deserves to be rejected.

6. On hearing learned counsels of both sides and on  perusal of the recitals of the F.I.R. it reveals that after marriage  the victim staying along with the applicants for four months,
 within four months there was no complaint as to the  ill-treatment at the hands of the present applicants.

Moreover,
 it reveals from the title clause of both the applications that only  the applicant Nos.1,2 and 3 in Criminal Application (APL)
 No.146/2021 are residing together, whereas the other  applicants in Criminal Application (APL) No.28/2021 are the
distant
relatives
. They are residing separately.

They have no  concerned regarding day to day home affairs of the informant  and her husband.
 7. Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code prescribed  punishment where a woman is subjected to cruelty by her  husband or his relatives.

sentences.text:
The explanation appended to the  provision defines cruelty in two parts, clause (a) refers to  willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive a  woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to  her life, limb or health (whether mental or physical); clause (b)
 refers to scope of the term which include harassment with a  view to coercing woman or her relative to meet any unlawful  926-apl146.21 & 28.21.odt 4/6  demand for any property or valuable security or on account of  failure to meet such demand.
A bare perusal of the F.I.R. and  the material placed on record
reveals that no specific  allegations are levelled against the applicants as to the demand  or the harassment.
General allegation is levelled against all the  applicants that they used to harass her after four months of the  marriage.

This aspect is recently considered by the Hon'ble  Apex Court in the case of Sanjay D. Jain and others vs. State of  Maharashtra in Special Leave Petition No.12584/2024 wherein  the Hon'ble Apex Court while considering the scope of Section  498 observed that the cruelty caused by the husband and his  family members should be of such a nature that it is inflicted  with an intention to cause grave injury or drive the victim to  commit suicide or inflict grave injury to herself, such  allegations are to be there.

entities.text: Sanjay D. Jain and others vs. State of  Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The omnibus statements made in  the complaint without any particular whatsoever would not be  sufficient to attract the offence punishable under Section 498A  of the Indian Penal Code.
8. Similar is the case in the present matter also.
There  are omnibus statements made in the complaint without any  particulars whatsoever.
A perusal of the F.I.R. indicates that  statements of a general nature have been made therein as  against the present applicants.

Except the general allegations,
 other statements of the relatives are also appeared to be  general in nature as well as without any particulars.
It is also  to be noted that for the purpose of constituting an offence  punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code  cruelty as indicated in the explanation to the said provision
must be stated to be inflicted.

These aspects are further  926-apl146.21 & 28.21.odt 5/6  considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mange  Ram Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and another, reported in  MANU/SC/1066/2025, wherein it is observed that "the family  members of the husband ought not to be unnecessarily roped  into criminal proceedings arising out of matrimonial discord.

entities.text: Mange  Ram Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and another, reported in  MANU/SC/1066/2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Court observed that it has become a recurring tendency to  implicate every member of the husband's family, irrespective of  their role or actual involvement, merely because a dispute has Vanita W/O Satish Katkar vs State Of Mah. Thr. Psops Mangarulpir ... on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87584175/
3  arisen between the spouses.

sentences.text: It was further held that where the  allegations are bereft of specific particulars, and particularly  where the relatives sought to be prosecuted are residing  separately or have had no connection with the matrimonial  home, allowing the prosecution to proceed would amount to an  abuse of the process of law.

The Apex Court further noted that  criminal law is not to be deployed as an instrument of  harassment, and that judicial scrutiny must be exercised to  guard against such misuse."
 9.

In the light of the above observations of the Hon'ble  Apex Court as already observed earlier that entire allegations  levelled against the present applicants are omnibus in nature,
 no specific instances are narrated as far as harassment at the  hands of present applicants are concerned, more particularly  the allegations as far as the applicants in Criminal Application  (APL) No.28/2021 are concerned, who are the distant relatives  never resided with the informant and her husband.

As far as  the husband is also concerned, absolutely no specific  allegations are levelled against him also to show that the  cruelty was of such a nature which drive her to commit suicide  or any grave injury is sustained by her or she was constrained  926-apl146.21 & 28.21.odt   to leave matrimonial house due to the said harassm  Therefore, no prima facie case is made out against  applicants.
In view of that, both the applications  allowed.

Accordingly, we proceed to pass following  ORDER (i) Criminal Application (APL) No.146/2021 and Criminal Application (APL) No.28/2021 are hereby allowed.
(ii) The First Information Report in connection with Crime No.1132/2020, registered with Police Station Mangrulpir, District Washim, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code is hereby quashed and set aside to the extent of applicants in both the applications.
(iii) Both the applications are disposed of.
(Nandesh S. Deshpande, J.) (Urmila Joshi-Phalke, J.) Wadode Signed by: Mr. Devendra Wadode Designation: PS To Honourable Judge Date: 07/11/2025 17:38:05
